title: Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape Flaw Allows Remote Code Execution
excerpt: Researchers have demonstrated a now-patched Ghostscript vulnerability that lets crafted file uploads escape the sandbox and run server commands.
body_html:
Security researchers have demonstrated a critical vulnerability in Ghostscript, a widely used interpreter on Linux servers that handles the conversion of uploaded PDFs, PostScript files, and images into different formats.

According to security firm pwn.ai, the now-patched flaw enables attackers to utilize specially crafted files to break out of the program's security sandbox. Once the security boundary is bypassed, the exploit allows the execution of arbitrary commands directly on the server processing the file uploads, often occurring without the host application invoking the interpreter directly.

Administrators and developers are advised to ensure their systems are updated with the latest security patches provided by Ghostscript to mitigate the risk of remote code execution.
